newsitem.title: FRANCE: Goldman tops list of M&A advisers in France -paper.
newsitem.headline: Goldman tops list of M&A advisers in France -paper.

text.p: U.S. investment firm Goldman Sachs topped the list of mergers and acquisitions advisers in France last year, dethroning French M&A specialist Lazard Freres, the newspaper La Tribune reported on Tuesday.

It said Goldman, which advised insurer Axa on the merger with UAP, the biggest deal of the year, handled deals totalling 107.5 billion francs, followed by Lazard with 106.4 billion, the paper said, citing figures compiled by newsletter Capital Finance.
Paribas was in third place with 105.5 billion francs of deals. Banexi-BNP and Rothschild & Cie ranked fourth and fifth.
Morgan Stanley, Societe Generale, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, CS First Boston and JP Morgan, in that order, also made the top 10.

After AXA-UAP, the largest deals in France in 1996 were the LVMH bid for duty free group DFS valuing the U.S. group at 21.9 billion francs, Suez unit Generale de Belgique's bid for Tractebel for 19.8 billion francs, and retailer Auchan's 19.5 billion franc takeover of Docks de France.
